Title: Boards
Overview: Boards provides a whiteboard workspace within Godot utilizing its built-in GraphEdit, GraphNode, and UI tools. Create Board assets and populate them with widgets on an infinite grid for planning and documentation. Boards can also be extended with custom widgets.
GettingStarted:
To create a new Board open the menu to create a new Resource and select KDTBoard as the type. When naming the file, choose between making a .tres, which stores data as readable text, or a .res, which stores data as binary. To open any Board simply double-click it and a tab for that Board will be made in the KDT Board Editor main screen.

When editing a Board the window is split into two sections. On the left is the grid where widgets can be placed and on the right is the widget inspector, notes area, and change history starting from when the Board was opened. To place widgets, right click the grid and select a widget from the popup menu. Drag the widget around to grid to move it. Widgets can also be locked to prevent moving by enabling the lock icon in the top right corner. To edit the contents of a widget, select the widget and the inspector will be populated with the widget's editable properties.

All widgets come with Base Properties for naming the widget, setting the font size of the widget name, changing the background color of the widget, and spawning/managing connection ports.

Ports allow widgets to be visually connected. Ports can be added either by using a preset or individually. Ports that are made from presets are marked blue in the list and can only be removed by changing the preset. Each port has a setting for the port name, position along the edge of the widget, size of the visual, color, and input/output setting of the port. Note that in order to connect ports one must be an input and the other an output. To disconnect, drag the connection off of an input port (empty circle).

In the top right corner of the grid are several tools. The window icon can be used to toggle between viewing the Board as an embedded tab or a floating window. The brush icon allows you to draw on the grid using right mouse (this creates a selectable Draw widget if one is not already selected). The magnifying glass icon opens the search menu where you can search for widgets by name and type. Clicking the widget name will scroll to that widget. The tools icon allows you to set Board settings.
MakingCustomWidgets:
To create your own custom widgets, you must extend certain classes and create corresponding scenes. The classes to extend are as follows:
  • KDTWidgetBase
  • KDTWidgetInspectorBase
  • KDTWidgetSaveDataBase
Make sure all classes you create are marked with the 'Tool' attribute. Look at the built-in subclasses to see examples.
WidgetClass:
Your widget class should inherit from KDTWidgetBase. This class will be responsible handling the data on your widget and is the script to attach to the root of the corresponding widget scene you create for it. You'll want to add getters and setters for the data to be modified by your widget inspector class.

The OnInitialize() virtual function is provided to handle initial setup for your widget.

You must also implement the Save(), Load(), and GetSaveDataClass(). The GetSaveDataClass() function returns the type of class to use for saving your widget data. The Save() and Load() functions should both call base first. Then, cast the save data parameter to the save data class you use in the GetSaveDataClass() function. Once cast, you can then set or get saved data.
SaveDataClass: To save additional data for your widget, make a class that inherits from KDTWidgetSaveDataBase. Add any number of public variables with the 'Export' attribute. Note that only certain types can be automatically serialized by Godot into Resources.
WidgetScene: Your widget scene is responsible for displaying the widget on the Board grid. It should inherit from GraphNode (which then gets changed by attaching your widget class) and also requires assigning a widget inspector scene in the Inspector. You can add any UI nodes for displaying information or providing interaction. Generally, trying to input information using the widget scene can lead to UI issues so creating an inspector is recommended. You should only give the root node one immediate child due to how GraphNodes work.
WidgetInspectorClass:
Your widget inspector class should inherit from KDTWidgetInspectorBase. The widget inspector is responsible for passing data from the widget inspector scene to the widget.

The OnInitialize() virtual function is provided to handle initial setup for the widget inspector. Within this function you should also cast the 'widget' variable to your widget class and subscribe data changes from your inspector scene UI to setters on the widget instance.

The OnRefresh() virtual function is provided to get data from the widget to repopulate the inspector UI. The 'widget' variable can be cast to your widget class to call getters.
WidgetInspectorScene: Your widget inspector scene is responsible for displaying interactable UI to pass data to your widget using your inspector class. This is the scene that should be assigned in your widget scene so it will automatically be constructed when clicking on the widget in a Board. Attach your widget inspector class script to the root node and construct the UI inside of the 'Add Here' node.
